answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can require identities to deposit slashable collateral in an escrow lagoon within a willow Merkle tree. Agents earn fee nectar by processing tasks, but provable double-signing burns their deposit. Attackers incur a verifiable capital cost per identity through locked principal and foregone yield. However, this design is limited by capital disparity, as wealthy adversaries can fund multiple identities while resource-poor honest agents are excluded.
